key_insight: GBClaw links agentic AI simulations with mechanistic analysis, revealing how defect hierarchies and metastable grain boundary structures influence sliding resistance in nickel.
engineering_relevance: Understanding how grain boundary structure controls shear resistance can inform microstructure engineering for improved deformation performance in polycrystalline materials.
method: Coordinate LLM-driven specialist agents, domain tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory.
Use dynamic replanning to connect systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis.
Compare sliding with and without secondary grain boundary misfit dislocations, then pursue researcher-guided follow-up calculations.
evidence_signal: Across 14 general asymmetric tilt grain boundaries in nickel, simulations identified diverse deformation modes and substantial shear-strength differences associated with secondary misfit dislocations.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the studied nickel boundaries, and resolving anomalous behavior required researcher-guided follow-up.
paper_title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
